stem: Which of the following nephron segments is impermeable to water while actively extruding sodium into the medullary interstitium?

options.label: A
options.text: Proximal convoluted tubule in the renal cortex
options.misconception: The bulk reabsorption site is being assigned the countercurrent multiplier role.
options.explanation: The proximal tubule reabsorbs most filtered solute and water isosmotically; the medullary gradient is built in the loop of Henle.

options.label: B
options.text: Descending limb of the loop of Henle in the medulla
options.misconception: The water-permeable limb is being confused with the salt-pumping limb.
options.explanation: The descending limb is freely water-permeable via aquaporins and loses water to the interstitium; it does not actively extrude sodium.

options.label: C
options.text: Ascending limb of the loop of Henle in the medulla
options.misconception: None; the ascending limb pumps Na+ without water following, raising medullary osmolarity.
options.explanation: The ascending limb is impermeable to water yet actively pumps Na+ into the interstitium, creating the hyperosmotic medulla of the countercurrent multiplier.

options.label: D
options.text: Distal convoluted tubule in the renal cortex
options.misconception: A downstream fine-tuning segment is being assigned the gradient-building role.
options.explanation: The distal tubule adjusts sodium under aldosterone control but does not generate the medullary osmolar gradient.

options.label: E
options.text: Cortical collecting duct in the renal medulla
options.misconception: The final urine-concentrating segment is being confused with the gradient generator.
options.explanation: The collecting duct reabsorbs water under ADH using the pre-existing medullary gradient; the ascending limb builds that gradient.

context: Learning objective: identify the countercurrent multiplier segment. The water-impermeable ascending limb extrudes Na+ (and urea contributes) to create medullary hyperosmolarity.
